definitions: A member of an ancient Jewish ascetic sect of the 1st century BC–1st century AD in Palestine, who lived in highly organized communities and held property in common. These people are generally regarded as the authors of the Dead Sea Scrolls.
A member of a Jewish sect of the Mishnaic period, who practiced an ascetic life and were concerned with ritual purity.
examples: The Essenes were known for their communal living.
Many scholars believe the Dead Sea Scrolls were written by the Essenes.
